conditions.condition_text: Zoom out to the 4H chart to analyze the larger point of view trend and develop a daily bias.
Top-down analysis provides the necessary conviction for trades on smaller timeframes.
Identify market structure (higher lows for bullish, lower highs for bearish) to confirm the overall trend bias.
Market structure defines the primary trend direction.
Identify Key Pivot Levels (KPLs), multi-touch points, or SMAs (50/200) on the larger timeframe.
These levels serve as points of interest for potential reversals or continuation.
Zoom into the 1H or 5M timeframe to gather more granular data and look for entry triggers.
Zooming in provides more data without changing the larger point of view bias.
Wait for the larger timeframe candle (e.g., 1H) to close, confirming the reversal or continuation intent.
The larger timeframe candle close provides the final confirmation of the trade direction.
The market must be in a clear uptrend or downtrend based on higher lows or lower highs.
Price must be near a Key Pivot Level (KPL), multi-touch point, or SMA (50/200).
Wait for volume to come in before looking for reactions near KPLs.
The entry must be confirmed by the close of the larger timeframe candle.
